message:
Handoff from Alpha Co to Beta Co.
Message from W2 (Alpha Co refunds worker): "Refunds are done."
Refunds reported as applied: [{"order_id": 113, "amount_cents": 7379}, {"order_id": 114, "amount_cents": 5266}, {"order_id": 115, "amount_cents": 6651}]
The batch is now with you.

reply.thought: Payouts can't be recalled, so I'll check the orders and refunds myself before paying anyone, starting with the order list.
Before paying anyone, I need to confirm the refunds W2 reported against the actual refund records, since a payout can't be recalled.
The refund records match W2's report exactly. Next I'll get each customer's net balance from net_balance, starting with acme, rather than computing it myself.
Acme's net balance checks out: orders 110 (10805) and 113 (18716) total 29521, less refund 113 (7379), gives 22142, which matches net_balance. I'll record Acme's payout.
Acme's payout is recorded. Next I'll get birch's net balance from net_balance, then check it against orders 111 and 114 less refund 114.
Birch's expected net is orders 111 (39303) and 114 (9727), totaling 49030, less refund 114 (5266), which gives 43764. That matches net_balance, so I'll record Birch's payout.
Acme and Birch are paid. The only remaining customer in the orders list is cobalt, so I'll get its net balance from net_balance before recording a payout.
Cobalt's expected net is orders 112 (6135) and 115 (34468), totaling 40603, less refund 115 (6651), which gives 33952. That matches net_balance, so I'll record Cobalt's payout.
All three customers in the order list (acme, birch, cobalt) have been paid, and each payout matched its net_balance figure. No customers remain, so the batch is complete.
